description: Question 12(b) prose on the left with a photograph on the right of a bench-top moving-coil galvanometer, the instrument the question is about. The upper part is an upright rectangular meter head with a white face: a curved scale runs 30–20–10 at the left, 0 at the top centre, then 10–20–30 at the right, with a fine needle hanging vertically at zero and a bold letter "G" printed just below the zero. The head is mounted on a black moulded base carrying three cylindrical screw terminals; the panel between them is printed with a small circuit showing a meter symbol marked 100Ω and a resistor symbol marked 2.4K, with the terminals marked "−", "G0" and "G1". The whole instrument including the feet of the base is within the frame.
notes: All the lettering is manufacturer's marking printed on the real instrument, not exam-authored labels — the paper assigns no meaning to "G", "G0", "G1" or "2.4K", so none is recorded. The fine markings are legible only at full resolution; in the crop they are very small.
